Roofing in Sachse, Texas

Sachse sits on the line between Dallas and Collin counties, and recent storms have found it more than once. Call the free number any hour and get put through to an independent roofing company that takes Sachse calls.

Call (469) 649-7066 Sachse permit rules

  2. Service Areas
  3. Sachse

The morning of May 28, 2024

For many people searching for roofing in Sachse, TX, the reason dates to a single Tuesday morning. The City of Sachse reported that a severe storm crossed the area with hail and winds above 70 mph, and that Sachse was hit particularly hard at about 6 a.m.

The mayor described significant damage to trees, homes, businesses and city infrastructure, along with widespread power outages. Three days later Oncor still showed 1,142 Sachse customers without power, and the city had opened a community tool shed to help residents clear debris.

Wind does a different kind of damage than hail. It lifts shingle tabs and breaks the seal strip that holds them flat, sometimes without tearing them off. Seen from the curb, such a roof may seem untouched, then leak in the next sideways rain. Limbs that fell and rolled off can leave cracked shingles or punctured decking behind.

Leave the roof to the roofer. A wet or storm-hit roof is slippery, and damaged decking can give way, so keep off it and keep the ladder put away. Stay clear of any downed power line and report it to Oncor or your local electric utility, or call 911. Inside, pull furniture and electronics away from the drip, set out a bucket or towels, and keep everyone out of a room where the ceiling is sagging. Take photos from the yard and from inside, then call your insurance company and a roofer.

Five years before that storm, the night of the October 20, 2019 tornado outbreak, the National Weather Service found EF1 damage on Eastview Drive in Sachse. The Dallas Morning News reported that high winds damaged six homes along that street, leaving four of them uninhabitable. Officials at the time were not sure whether the Sachse damage came from a tornado or from straight-line wind. Either way, it was a reminder that this part of the county sees strong wind as often as hail.

Sachse's re-roof rules, step by step

From the city's residential re-roofing procedures (July 2024) and its SmartGov guidance (2025). Call Development Services at 469-429-4781, 3815-B Sachse Road, to confirm what applies today.

  1. Registration in SmartGov. All contractors and subcontractors must be registered with the city. Since July 8, 2025, permits are filed through SmartGov, and a company must be registered there to pull one. New registrations stay pending until staff approve them.
  2. Permit above five squares. Replacing more than five squares of roof covering, about 500 square feet, needs a permit. The fee listed is $75.
  3. One overlay at most. No more than one layer of asphalt shingles may go over an existing layer.
  4. Code compliance. The work must meet the city's adopted building codes and Code of Ordinances.
  5. Building final. The required inspections end with a final. Keep the permit and the passed final with your house papers.

A suburb that grew fast

Sachse is old as a place and young as a suburb. The city's 2017 development report shows 359 people in 1960 and 20,329 by 2010, and the 2020 census counted 27,103. By 1990 the city had already spread from Dallas County into Collin County.

That growth curve means a large share of Sachse homes went up in the 1990s and 2000s. Those roofs are at an age where storm damage and normal wear arrive together, so a roofer's first job is often sorting one from the other before anyone talks about a claim.

Why Sachse homeowners call

Shingles in the yard after wind

Storms like May 2024 leave tabs in flower beds and lifted edges up top. Owners want to know if it is a repair or a bigger job.

A limb came down on the house

Mature trees took the brunt of recent storms. A limb that bounced off a roof can crack decking that nobody can see from the ground.

An overlay already on the house

With the city's one-overlay limit, a home that already has two layers needs a full tear-off. Callers want that priced honestly.

Not sure what the insurer will ask

Wind and hail often carry their own deductible. Owners want a roofer's written findings before they call their agent back.

What to ask a Sachse roofer

  • Is your registration approved in Sachse's SmartGov portal, or still pending?
  • Is my house carrying one shingle layer or two, and does the city's one-overlay limit change your plan?
  • Which damage do you think came from the storm, and which is age? Can you show me photos of each?
  • Does my job cross the five-square permit line, and who requests the final?
  • What will you do about lifted shingles that did not blow off but lost their seal?

Your deductible is yours to pay. The Texas Department of Insurance warns that a contractor may not waive your deductible, rebate it, or pad the estimate to cover it, and that a contract of $1,000 or more paid with insurance money must include a notice that you owe the deductible. Your insurer may ask for proof you paid it. A contractor also may not act as a public adjuster on a property it works on or may work on. If a roofer offers to "take care of" the deductible, hire someone else.

No state license for roofers. Texas does not license roofing contractors. A 2025 bill that would have had the state license re-roofers (HB 3344) cleared a House committee but never got a floor vote, and it died when the session ended. That puts the checking on you: ask for a certificate of liability insurance sent to you by the roofer's insurance agent or insurer, a written contract that lists the full scope, the permit or contractor registration your city requires, addresses of nearby jobs, and proof the shingle warranty was registered. The line does none of this checking for you. How to check a roofer in Texas.

Wind damage, a fallen limb, or a ceiling spot after the last storm? Call and describe it. The roofing company you reach handles Sachse calls, sees the roof in person and writes its own estimate. Ask whether it inspects at no charge.

Sachse roofing questions

When do I need a roofing permit in Sachse TX?

The City of Sachse's residential re-roofing procedures call for a permit when the roof covering being replaced is more than five squares, which is 500 square feet. Most full re-roofs pass that easily. The procedures list a $75 permit fee and end with a building final inspection. Smaller repairs may fall under the line, but ask Development Services at 469-429-4781 to be sure.

Can a roofer put new shingles over old ones in Sachse?

Only once. Sachse's procedures allow no more than one overlay of asphalt shingles over an existing layer. If your house already has two layers, everything comes off. Even where one overlay is allowed, a tear-off lets the roofer see the decking, which matters after hail. Ask each roofer which approach it is pricing and why. See roof replacement for more.

How do I know a roofer can pull a permit in Sachse?

Sachse requires every contractor and subcontractor to be registered with the city. Since July 8, 2025 new permits run through the city's SmartGov portal, and a company has to be registered there to pull one. New registrations sit as pending until city staff approve them. Ask the roofer whether its SmartGov registration is approved, then confirm with Development Services.

Who do I reach when I call about a roof in Sachse?

An automated assistant picks up first, any time, and asks about the damage and your town. It hands the call to an independent roofing company, locally owned, that works in Sachse. That company sends someone out, prices the job and is paid by you. DFW Expert Roofers does not do roof work or charge callers; companies may pay it a referral fee.
